chats.answer:
Look for a charger whose two-port power allocation explicitly gives the laptop 65 W while the phone is connected. A charger labeled “65 W” usually means 65 W total, not 65 W for the laptop plus extra for the phone. A 100 W dual-USB-C charger with a documented 65 W + 30 W split is a good target.

My pick is the Anker Prime 100 W, model A2688. Anker explicitly specifies 65 W from USB-C1 and 35 W from USB-C2 when both are in use, so it meets your requirement without relying on a vague combined-wattage claim. 
service.anker.com

Anker Prime 100W 3-Port USB GaN Wall Charger

$69.99

B&H Photo

Model A2688. Compact, folding plug; laptop gets 65 W and phone gets up to 35 W.

Plug the laptop into the upper USB-C port (C1) and the phone into C2. Use a 5 A e-marked USB-C cable rated for 100 W or 240 W for the laptop; an ordinary 60 W cable cannot deliver the full 65 W. Cables are not included. 
Anker US

I assumed your laptop accepts standard USB-C Power Delivery and your phone needs no more than 35 W. The 65 W figure is the power available to the laptop, not a guarantee it will continuously draw that much. I verified the published allocation, not through hands-on testing; I also haven't checked whether your particular phone can reach its fastest charging mode on C2.
